**0086 IS LANDED AT `3fcc71a` AND IS OPEN PENDING dc's REVIEW -- the suite hang hv hit, and it is the sharpest false green this project has produced.**

**WHAT HAPPENED.** hv ran `dvb test all` from a terminal at 21:26Z. It printed `ok 652` at 21:35Z and then nothing, and hv interrupted it at 05:48Z: quiet 8h13m, elapsed 8h22m, exit 141. Test 653 is `tests/unit/helpers.bats:857`, the read-only `replace_file` arm. `rename_staged` (lib/helpers:536) renamed with a bare `mv`, and POSIX mv PROMPTS when the destination exists, permissions do not allow writing it, and stdin is a tty. Measured under a pty, verbatim: `override r--r--r--  matts/staff for /.../f? (y/n [n])`. No tty, no prompt, rc 0.

**WHY IT IS THE SHARPEST ONE: THE PROMPT IS TTY-GATED AND NOTHING THAT NORMALLY RUNS THE SUITE HAS A TTY.** Every agent run and both CI jobs passed, including the 1372 ok at `e3f1231`. Nothing was wrong with that count -- the run could not reach the condition. **A false green that is green for everyone able to observe it**, and the one class of runner it hangs for is the one that gets no output to explain it.

**THE REACH IS WIDER THAN THE SUITE.** `replace_file` and `sed_inplace` are how devbin rewrites a file whose mode it does not own -- the version stamp, a dated note, a generated view, the fleet document. Any of those replacing a read-only file from a terminal blocked identically. The test is where it was found, not the limit of it.

**FIX:** `mv -f`, the form `lib/install:379` already used; those are the only two mv calls in the runtime. Arm driven RED FIRST at its own assertion naming `lib/helpers:549`. `tests/unit/helpers.bats` 76 ok, 0 not ok. `lib/helpers` is VENDORED, so it goes in the next sweep's pre-notice.

**TWO LIMITS I DECLARED RATHER THAN SOLVED, and dc is asked to attack both.** (1) The arm is LEXICAL -- it cannot tell `-f` from `-if`, and I could not drive the prompt behaviourally because a bats run has no tty. **I tried twice with `script` and failed, so the block is INFERRED from the measured prompt and not reproduced, and it is written down that way.** (2) `tests/` is excluded deliberately: nineteen bare `mv` calls there, all moving files the test just created, so none can prompt today -- but a test moving over a read-only fixture would hang the suite identically and the arm would not see it.

**THE CLASS IS NOT CENSUSED AND IS UNASSIGNED.** Any external command devbin runs that can block on a terminal: a prompt, a PAGER, an editor, a credential or host-key ask. **`git` paging when stdout is a tty is the first candidate and nobody has checked it.** hv wanted devbin-cc on this; **devbin-cc is not reachable as a session** (ListAgents shows devbin-dc and four other-estate nodes only), so the assignment is written and undelivered, and the census is nobody's until hv says.

**0085 IS REVIEWED AND BACK WITH dc, NOT CLOSED.** Four items, sent 21:42Z and 21:49Z. Its code is right at all six sites; its coverage is not. dc found the core hole itself first (the class arm tests the `--source` FLAG while `note_invocation` prints only a non-empty VALUE). vc added the discriminating pair on the landed bytes -- the identical `--source ""` mutation is KILLED at `lib/resolve:915` and SURVIVES at `lib/cmd/fullcycle:772` and `bin/.devbin/cmd/test:32` -- plus the wrong-site mutant that defeats dc's proposed non-empty check, the proof that fullcycle IS drivable (a `DEVBIN_LIB` shim; dc had written it off), the anchor-x2 problem in M1/M2, and the class arm's silent drop of an unterminated span. Six mutants re-driven to dc's matrix exactly.

**WITH hv AND UNANSWERED: the D19 wrapper-flag defect and AC-3.2.** Both are written up with options and a recommendation for the bounce.
